en: He gathered many men of the people.
The keenest of the clear-eyed,
The sage who had seen much,
The impartial man who could untie a knot,
Rousing them all from the roots,
He left none of them behind.
The man who would swing an axe when challenged,
The man who could devise broad counsel,
The narrow-minded man of wicked thought,
The master fit for every task,
Leaving aside the timid and taking the heroes,
The champion who observed with calm care,
Chyng Tengir gathered them without leaving one behind,
He raised a cry and began to speak,
Speaking softly but laying down his words firmly:
Zhelzhetpes, who traveled between the sides,
No soul could pass Zhelzhetpes,
Say that Zhelzhetpes must go between them,
Say that he must send word across the world.
Let him take six mules and horses,
Let him swiftly take provisions for the road,
One who, when he gulps, is never sated with blood,
One who spares no life when fighting,
If you ask for his single head,
One who could match countless men,
Let him take a wrestler-hero at his side.
The four corners of the round world,
Let him roam all four circuits,
The five corners of the entire world,
Let him mark them and travel through them.
Let him find a mountain to strike against,
Let him find a hostile enemy to fight.
Let him find a soul to face him head-on,
Those who dwell in the Ala-Too,
Whose six generations of forefathers were khans,
Who answered to no one in the world,
Who multiplied whenever they were killed,
With Khydyr himself following them.
